display_name: Nav2 + MoveIt (ROS2 navigation + motion planning stack)
install_tell: ros2 launch nav2_bringup tb3_simulation_launch.py; ros2 launch moveit2_tutorials demo.launch.py; ros2 launch rosbridge_server rosbridge_websocket_launch.xml
misconfig_patterns: Nav2 + MoveIt action servers have NO native authentication — any caller on the ROS graph can send a goal that moves the robot
rosbridge_server (port 9090) bridges all ROS topics/services to JSON-over-WebSocket with NO auth by default — the standard way Nav2/MoveIt reach the internet
rosbridge_server /topics endpoint enumerates every topic name — reveals robot capability surface without subscribing
DDS discovery on UDP 7400+ allows direct ROS graph join from any IP that can reach those ports — bypasses rosbridge entirely
SROS2 / DDS-Security is opt-in and rarely enabled — ROS_SECURITY_ENABLE=false is the default
/move_base_simple/goal is a legacy ROS1-bridged topic some deployments retain — single PoseStamped publish moves the robot
Co-deployed web_video_server (port 8080) on the same host provides live camera feedback, completing the teleop loop
ROS_DOMAIN_ID 0 is the default — multiple unrelated robots on the same network segment can see each other's traffic
rosapi service exposes service-list / param-list introspection without subscription (read-only enumeration channel)
rosbridge_server has no rate-limiting or per-client quota by default

active_probe.false_positive_check: rosbridge_server /topics returns a JSON object with a 'topics' array of topic names. Nav2 confirmation: presence of at least one of /navigate_to_pose, /follow_path, /spin, /wait, or /move_base in the topic list. MoveIt confirmation: presence of /move_group/goal or /compute_ik or /compute_fk. Reject if /topics is missing or returns non-JSON — likely an unrelated websocket service. Reject Foxglove handshakes that lack the rosbridge JSON contract.

shodan_dorks.notes: Nav2 and MoveIt themselves do not expose HTTP — they are reachable through rosbridge_server (port 9090, JSON-over-WS) or DDS (UDP 7400+). Per Insight #93, one variant has no port: constraint to catch reverse-proxied / non-default-port deployments. Population is bounded above by the rosbridge population; expect a single-digit-percent fraction expose Nav2 or MoveIt topics specifically. Body markers /move_base and /move_group are the cleanest identity signal because they appear in the rosbridge /topics HTTP response.

deployment_tells: Docker image osrf/ros:humble-desktop or ros:jazzy-ros-base as the base layer
Launch file references nav2_bringup, moveit2_tutorials, rosbridge_server
Co-deployed siblings on same IP (shadow-sweep priorities): foxglove_bridge :8765, web_video_server :8080, rosapi :9091, DDS discovery UDP :7400+
Warehouse robot deployments: Locus Robotics, 6 River Systems, Fetch Robotics, OTTO Motors
Agricultural: Naio Technologies, FarmWise, Carbon Robotics
Collaborative arm integrators (MoveIt): Universal Robots UR5/UR10/UR16, Franka Emika Panda, Kuka iiwa, ABB GoFa
Academic / demo: PAL Robotics TIAGo, Clearpath Husky / Jackal, Isaac ROS reference stacks
Cert subject-CN patterns: robot.<org>, fleet.<org>, ros.<org>, nav.<org>, teleop.<org>
ROS_DOMAIN_ID env var visible in process listings is the per-fleet partition key
tf2 transform tree topics (/tf, /tf_static) co-publish with Nav2/MoveIt — secondary identity confirmation
pivot_paths: GET /topics via rosbridge → capability fingerprint (which Nav2/MoveIt actions are running)
GET /services via rosbridge → service-list enumeration (planner type, controller type)
GET /nodes via rosbridge → node-list including planner_server, controller_server, behavior_server, move_group
GET /params via rosbridge → frequently leaks robot model, map filename, costmap parameters
Foxglove bridge :8765 channel list → same enumeration over Foxglove WebSocket protocol
Shadow-sweep on same IP: 8080 (web_video_server camera), 8765 (foxglove_bridge), 9091 (rosapi), UDP 7400+ (DDS)
tf2 topic /tf via rosbridge → reveals robot kinematic chain (link names, joint names) without moving anything
TLS cert subject-CN on :443 → VisorGraph operator-portfolio pivot (fleet operator attribution)
do_not_call: POST/publish to /navigate_to_pose/_action/send_goal — commands the robot to drive to a pose
POST/publish to /move_base_simple/goal — legacy ROS1 single-publish goal — moves the robot
POST/publish to /move_group/_action/send_goal — commands arm motion planning + execution
POST/publish to /execute_trajectory/_action/send_goal — executes a planned arm trajectory
POST/publish to /cmd_vel — direct velocity command, bypasses planners
POST/publish to /joint_trajectory_controller/* — direct joint command, bypasses MoveIt
rosbridge advertise + publish on any control topic — lets caller advertise a new publisher and command the robot
Service call /clear_costmap — wipes safety map state
Service call /reinitialize_global_localization — destroys AMCL pose belief
data_class: robot capability surface + kinematic chain + real-time sensor stream when subscribed; primary harm is unauthenticated motion command (kinetic-impact safety hazard), not user PII; map data and joint names can reveal facility layout and machine identity
restraint_notes: Identity probe = GET /topics on rosbridge only (read-only schema enumeration)
Capability list (/navigate_to_pose, /follow_path, /move_group/goal in /topics) is the finding — sending a goal is the harm
Subscribing to camera, lidar, joint-state topics pulls live bandwidth and is operator-visible — channel list is sufficient at Stage 0c
/clear_costmap and /reinitialize_global_localization are read-named but state-changing — never call
DDS direct-graph join (UDP 7400+) is a possible probe channel — keep behind discipline: subscribing joins the graph and is visible to ros2 node list on the host

Insight #40 (auth-on-default shifts rightward): ROS2 has added SROS2 / DDS-Security across recent releases but adoption is the slow part — track production deployments adopting ROS_SECURITY_ENABLE=true
Severity rationale: a confirmed exposed Nav2 stack is remote-robot-control on the public internet — the open state is the finding, calling is unacceptable harm

version_history_auth_relevant.ROS1 (Kinetic/Melodic/Noetic, 2016-2025): no native auth; rosmaster on 11311 was the single coordinator; legacy systems still deployed
version_history_auth_relevant.ROS2 Foxy (2020): DDS replaces rosmaster; SROS2 / DDS-Security available but opt-in
version_history_auth_relevant.ROS2 Humble (2022): Nav2 1.x stable; MoveIt2 1.x stable; rosbridge_server ports forward to ROS2
version_history_auth_relevant.ROS2 Iron / Jazzy (2023-2024): improved SROS2 tooling but default-off remains the rule
version_history_auth_relevant.rosbridge_suite v2.0.0+ (2024): ROS2 support consolidated; no auth added by default
version_history_auth_relevant.ROS2 Rolling (continuous): SROS2 documentation expanded; field adoption lags docs
